rationale: This empirical study examines farmer water allocation practices, collective irrigation turns and crop-demand relative water supply across three agricultural rice irrigation systems in Central Luzon, Philippines. It concerns agricultural irrigation rather than household or community water or sanitation service access (E07).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2 because the study fails Criterion 1 (pure agricultural irrigation for rice crop production with no household or community drinking water or sanitation service access, E07).

evidence_quotes.quote: WATER MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES AND PRACTICES AT THE TERTIARY LEVEL: THREE PHILIPPINE IRRIGATION SYSTEMS
This research aimed to describe and understand practices used to obtain and allocate water in a large Philippine irrigation system and two small ones.
Direct seeding of the dry season rice crop was directly related to RWS, extra water being substituted for costly weed control measures.
